title: Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan
author: T
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Jensen Huang told Nvidia employees on Tuesday that the chipmaker’s leadership structure makes conventional CEO succession planning unnecessary, CNBC reported. In his first staff meeting since returning as CEO, Huang pointed to the executives who already lead different parts of the company. He argued that a traditional succession process could introduce unnecessary hierarchy into an organization built around direct access to its founder.

The timing gave his remarks particular weight. Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation on November 12 and appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO while the board began a search for a permanent successor. On November 23, the board unanimously reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and director. The episode gave Nvidia a real-world test of how it operates during an abrupt leadership change. NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition

Huang’s argument reflects how he runs Nvidia. He has said that more than 60 executives report directly to him, many of them in engineering. That structure brings technical leaders close to decisions that span chips, networking, and software. It also puts Huang at the center of decisions that cut across those groups. That coordinating role matters for a company selling complete AI computing systems, where choices about one component can affect the roadmap for the entire platform.

For customers and partners, the practical question is who can make those decisions during a longer transition. Cloud providers commit capital around Nvidia’s platform roadmaps, and suppliers plan around its production schedules. A board can prepare for that scenario privately by identifying who would own product priorities, customer commitments, and capital allocation if the CEO became unavailable.

Kress’s appointment showed that Nvidia could put an experienced executive in charge quickly. The longer-term question is how the company would carry forward the work Huang does across engineering, strategy, and customer relationships. That is the part of succession planning that matters most for Nvidia.
